steps.message: client.py is shared — `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` and points them at `https://reports.example.com`. Hardcoding `verify=False` there would also turn off certificate validation on the nightly production finance export, which isn't the self-signed endpoint you're working around.

questions.question: client.py serves both staging and the prod finance export. How should verify be scoped?

options.label: Env-gated, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env flag read in client.py (default True), and set it to false in scripts/sync_staging.py. Staging stops failing on the self-signed cert; export_prod.py keeps full verification.
options.preview:
client.py
  VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") not in {"0", "false", "False"}
  requests.get(..., timeout=10, verify=VERIFY_TLS)

scripts/sync_staging.py
  os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")

options.label: Hardcode verify=False
options.description: Exactly as asked: verify=False on both requests.get calls in client.py. Simplest diff, but the production export also stops validating certificates and urllib3 will emit InsecureRequestWarning on every prod run.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Point verify at the staging cert/CA bundle path via an env var rather than disabling validation. Keeps MITM protection everywhere, but needs the cert file available to whoever runs the script.
